why: Every effect sought since SeedLM-6 has been 1-5 tasks, but the noise of the comparisons was never measured directly: same-recipe runs differed by up to 9 of 139 teacher tasks, paired fine-tune differences were +4, +6, -2. The research report (reports/SeedLM 다음 발전 방향 조사.md, roadmap item 1) puts measurement resolution first
part_a_split: the extra pool's training part (434 real tasks with reference solutions, no development-fifth or MBPP+ task) becomes the diagnostic and calibration split, two folds by a hash of the task id (data/seedlm/diagnostic_split.json). It is training-side data: coders saw some of these descriptions, so it calibrates selection and judges, not coder generalization
part_b_noise: control-against-control pairs that differ only in the fine-tune seed (batch order; same base, same synthetic draw, same data): for each base s12-a1..a3, the existing s34-o<k> (seed 0) and two new fine-tunes with seeds 1 and 2 (s40-o<k>s1, s40-o<k>s2), 400 steps each. Measured per pair: the difference and the number of discordant tasks D, for the coder alone (held-out teacher 139; development 94, lenient and strict) and for the system (engine plus the coder, pyx_override; development, lenient and strict). Also the from-scratch same-recipe seed triples already cached (s12-a1..a3, s12-b1..b3). Reported: the standard deviation s of paired differences, mean D, and the number of seed pairs needed to detect 2.5 and 5 tasks at 80% power (R = (2.8 s / delta)^2)
part_c_contracts: a third judge, contract-strict: probe inputs are kept only if they satisfy an input contract inferred from the task's three asserts (types, element types, signs, sortedness, small value sets such as {0, 1}, string character classes, equal lengths, an integer argument equal to a sequence's length); a program fails if it differs from the reference on an in-domain probe. Validated on the training split by re-reading a sample of the remaining conflicts; then the main system is judged once on the development fifth (counts only)
choice: measurement only; no method is adopted or rejected here
note: the fine-tunes run while lighter analysis jobs use the CPU; results do not depend on speed (fixed seeds, fixed thread count)

outcome.part_c: training split, engine answers that pass the asserts (320): plain strict passes 271, contract-strict 288 (18 conflicts resolved, 1 new); of 10 remaining conflicts read: 4 real errors, 2 grey (tie order, a definition's convention), 4 artifacts, of which 2 (a three-value domain, single characters) were then covered by contract properties. Development fifth, the main system (engine + s5-var, pyx_override): 69 lenient, 58 strict, 57 contract-strict; engine alone 65, 56, 55 (reports/seedlm/holdout4_s5-var_strict.json). On real development tasks the in-domain probes found one more real difference than they removed artifacts: the true score sits at the strict end, not midway
outcome.part_b: reports/seedlm/seedlm40_noise.json. Fine-tune controls from one base, seeds 0/1/2 (9 coders): the system under the strict and contract judges moves by 0-1 task between seeds (mean discordant tasks 0-0.7), under the lenient judge by up to 2; the coder alone moves by up to 6 on the development fifth (s 0.8-4.3) and up to 5 on the held-out teacher tasks (s 2.2-3.6, 7-14 discordant tasks). From-scratch 40-minute seed triples: coder alone on teacher tasks s 2.5-4.9 with 23-30 discordant tasks; the system under the lenient judge moves by up to 4 (s 2.2-2.9). Every control system scores 56-59 strict and 56-58 contract-strict, the same as the adopted system (58, 57)
outcome.reading: Under a judge that checks behaviour, the system's score hardly depends on which coder it uses: the engine and the coder's tie-breaking set it, and the gains that coders seemed to add under the lenient judge were largely coincidental passes. Coder-level comparisons need about 3 seed pairs to see 5 tasks and about 11 to see 2.5 on the teacher tasks; earlier single comparisons of +2 to +3 were inside this noise
